worked_solution:
The first three terms of the binomial expansion for $(1+x)^{n}$ are given by

$$
(1+x)^{n}=1+nx+\frac{n(n-1)}{2!}{x}^{2}+⋯.
$$

By substituting $x=6t$ and $n=7$ into the above formula, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}{(1+6t)}^{7} & =1+7\cdot 6t+\frac{7(7-1)}{2!}\cdot {(6t)}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1+42t+\frac{7\cdot 6}{2}\cdot 36{t}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1+42t+21\cdot 36{t}^{2}+⋯ \\  & =1+42t+756{t}^{2}+⋯.\end{aligned}
$$
